title: too y enough (demasiado y suficiente)
short: The suitcase is too heavy. The room isn't big enough. We haven't got enough towels.

story.title: Demasiado y suficiente
story.text: ==too== = demasiado (más de lo que quieres). ==enough== = suficiente, lo bastante.

examples.es: La habitación es lo bastante grande.

story.title: ¿Dónde van?
story.text: too va ==delante== del adjetivo. enough va ==detrás== del adjetivo y ==delante== del nombre.

story.title: too much y too many
story.text: Delante de un nombre: ==too much== + incontable (luggage, noise, traffic) y ==too many== + plural (people, bags).

story.title: very no es too
story.text: ==very== = muy (puede estar bien). ==too== = demasiado: hay un ==problema==.

examples.t: The hotel is very expensive, but it's lovely.
examples.es: El hotel es muy caro, pero es precioso.

examples.t: The hotel is too expensive. Let's go.
examples.es: El hotel es demasiado caro. Vámonos.

examples.t: The bed isn't big enough for two.
examples.es: La cama no es lo bastante grande para dos.

story.title: Así en español, así en inglés
story.text: «Demasiado» va delante de todo: demasiado caro, demasiada gente. En inglés: ==too== expensive pero ==too many== people. «Bastante grande» = big ==enough==, con enough detrás.

story.title: Errores típicos
story.text:
❌ too much expensive ✅ ==too== expensive
❌ enough big ✅ big ==enough==
❌ too much people ✅ too ==many== people
❌ The hotel is too nice! ✅ The hotel is ==very== nice!

story.title: Truco
story.text: enough es educado: se pone ==detrás== del adjetivo y deja pasar al nombre ==delante==: old enough, enough money. Se pronuncia «inaf».

compare.es: En español «demasiado» va siempre delante y concuerda (demasiado caro, demasiada gente, demasiados turistas). «Suficiente / bastante» suele ir delante del adjetivo: «bastante grande».
compare.target: En inglés too va delante del adjetivo (too expensive); con nombres, too much (incontable) o too many (plural). Enough va detrás del adjetivo (big enough) y delante del nombre (enough towels). Too siempre indica un problema; para «muy», very.

errors.why: Delante de un adjetivo, solo too.
Too indica un problema. Para elogiar, very.

exercises.q: This suitcase is ___ heavy. I can't lift it.
The room isn't ___.
There are ___ people at the gate.
There's ___ noise in the street.
We haven't got ___ time for breakfast.
It's ___ expensive. Let's find another hotel.
exercises.why: Delante de adjetivo, solo too (nunca too much).

exercises.q: The hotel is ___ nice! We love it.
exercises.why: Para elogiar, very. Too indica un problema.

exercises.q: Is the water warm ___ to swim?
My grandson isn't old ___ to drive.
exercises.es: Mi nieto no tiene edad para conducir.
exercises.why: No tiene edad suficiente: not old enough.

exercises.q: I've got too ___ bags for one person.
exercises.es: Llevo demasiadas bolsas para una sola persona.

exercises.q: There isn't ___ milk for everyone.
exercises.es: No hay leche suficiente para todos.
exercises.why: Enough delante del nombre: enough milk.

exercises.q: You eat too ___ sugar!
The bed isn't big enough ___ two people.
exercises.es: La cama no es lo bastante grande para dos personas.

exercises.q: It's too cold ___ go to the beach.
exercises.es: Hace demasiado frío para ir a la playa.

exercises.q: The coffee is ___ hot. I can't drink it.
exercises.es: El café quema demasiado. No puedo tomármelo.

exercises.q: The room is too small.
answer: The room is not big enough.

exercises.q: The taxi isn't cheap enough.
The water is too cold.
answer: The water is not warm enough.

exercises.q: My grandson isn't old enough to drive.
answer: My grandson is too young to drive.
My grandson's too young to drive.

exercises.q: The music isn't quiet enough.
There are too much tourists in summer.
I've got too many luggage.
We haven't got enought money.
exercises.why: Se escribe enough, sin t final.

exercises.q: It's to hot in this room.
The flat is very small for four people. We need a bigger one.
exercises.why: Es un problema (no caben): too small.

exercises.es: La habitación no es lo bastante grande

exercises.q: No tenemos suficientes toallas.
answer: We have not got enough towels.
We do not have enough towels.

exercises.q: Hay demasiada gente.
It's too expensive for us.

exercises.context: En el hotel pasas frío por la noche. Lo dices en recepción.
options: Excuse me, my room isn't warm enough.
Excuse me, my room isn't enough warm.
Excuse me, my room is too much cold.
exercises.answer: Excuse me, my room isn't warm enough.

exercises.context: Tu amiga quiere comprarse un bolso precioso, pero es carísimo.
options: It's lovely, but it's too expensive.
It's lovely, but it's too much expensive.
It's lovely, but it's enough expensive.
exercises.answer: It's lovely, but it's too expensive.

exercises.why: too delante; enough detrás del adjetivo y delante del nombre.
